$comment: HUP gate g3-licence: licence inventory for everything Citrate Core ships in its installer, downloads on first run, or bundles as text (knowledge corpus, reviewed skills).

Checked by scripts/licence-inventory.mjs against the bundle configs, components/toolchain-bundle.json, templates/deps.lock.json, skills.lock and (with --corpus) a staged knowledge corpus. The review and the draft source offer are in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
covers: externalBin:<path> and resource:<path> (tauri.bundle-*.conf.json), toolchain:<name>, library:<name>, skills:<label>, corpus:<source id>, planned:<name> (not shipped yet).

review: ok = what ships meets the licence's notice obligations; action = a known gap with a concrete fix; owner = needs an owner or counsel decision. Commits and versions for corpus and skills sources live in the corpus manifest and skills.lock, not here (one source of truth).
Nothing in this file is legal advice. sign_off stays pending until the owner or counsel signs the review.

app.name: Citrate Core
app.note: The app is source-available under BUSL-1.1. Copyleft tools are separate programs it runs as subprocesses or downloads on request; none is linked into the app.

components.name: citrate node (citrate-chain)
components.gap: The citrate-chain LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 while the federation NOTICE lists citrate-chain under BUSL-1.1; one of them should change.

components.name: node-agent (citrate-node-agent)
components.note: Third-party crate notices are generated by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs into src-tauri/licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (third_party_notices; generator choice pending owner sign-off, LICENCE_REVIEW 4.7).

components.name: mem-mcp memory daemon (citrate-memories)
components.note: RocksDB is dual GPL-2.0 / Apache-2.0 upstream; Citrate uses it under Apache-2.0. Third-party crate notices are generated by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs into src-tauri/licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (third_party_notices; generator choice pending owner sign-off, LICENCE_REVIEW 4.7).

components.name: comms-member-daemon (citrate-comms)
components.note: Third-party crate notices are generated by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs into src-tauri/licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (third_party_notices; generator choice pending owner sign-off, LICENCE_REVIEW 4.7).

components.name: cluster-daemon (citrate-cluster)
components.note: Third-party crate notices are generated by scripts/third-party-notices.mjs into src-tauri/licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt (third_party_notices; generator choice pending owner sign-off, LICENCE_REVIEW 4.7).

components.name: Hermes agent sidecar (citrate-agent-runtime, bundled as binaries/hermes)
components.gap: The citrate-agent-runtime LICENSE file is Apache-2.0 while the federation NOTICE lists it under BUSL-1.1.

components.name: llama.cpp (llama-server and its dylibs)
components.note: The llama runtime tarball also carries LICENSE-llama.cpp.txt beside the dylibs.

components.name: Kubo (ipfs) 0.42.0
components.note: Upstream release binary. Older code is MIT only (upstream LICENSE explains the transition); both texts ship.

components.name: BAAI bge-base-en-v1.5 embedding model
components.note: The model card declares MIT; the text is the FlagEmbedding repository LICENSE (BAAI's code and model home). models/bge-base-en-v1.5-gguf is the same weights (revision a5beb1e3) converted to GGUF f16 by llama.cpp's converter (scripts/build-bge-gguf.sh) for the embedding llama-server Hermes ranks tools with.

components.name: Gemma 4 E4B-it, Q4_0 GGUF (T0 model)
components.note: Bundled only by tauri.bundle-node.conf.json (the release workflow); bundle-lite builds download the same file on first run. Both model cards state Apache-2.0 (checked 2026-10-04).

components.name: Contract templates (HUP-S6.2)
components.note: Citrate's own contract templates; every Solidity source carries an SPDX MIT header so members may use the rendered contracts freely. Pinned libraries (OpenZeppelin, Solady, forge-std) are separate entries.

components.name: Third-party licence texts (this inventory's texts)
components.note: src-tauri/licenses/*, bundled so every notice travels with the app.

components.name: Reviewed third-party skills (staged from skills.lock)
components.note: Aggregate; each source is its own skills:<label> entry below.

components.name: Hermes knowledge corpus (format citrate-corpus/2)
components.note: Aggregate; each source is its own corpus:<id> entry below. The corpus carries NOTICE.md (per-source upstream, commit, licence, attribution, changes) and manifest.json.

components.name: Trail of Bits skills
components.source_offer: Adapted skills (executables stripped) are offered under CC BY-SA 4.0; the unmodified source is upstream at the commit in skills.lock.
components.note: Owner decision D-20 (2026-09-30): redistribute with attribution and a note of changes. ShareAlike applies to the adapted skill files, not to the app (a collection).

components.name: frontend-skills
components.gap: The top-level MIT grant is a README statement with no LICENSE file (HUP-S3.6, A18). impeccable and frontend-design ship their own LICENSE and NOTICE inside skills-bundle; the hyperframes Apache text ships here. Owner: add a LICENSE file upstream or confirm the README grant.

components.name: Hermes agent skills (NousResearch hermes-agent)
components.note: Rewritten at intake (strict loader, owner decision 2026-10-01); MIT permits modification with the notice kept.

components.name: Gradient Papers v3 and AGENTILE.md
components.gap: v0.5.0: gradient-papers deferred to 0.5.1 by owner decision 2026-10-06 (no repository yet, so no fetchable commit); agentile now records a clean commit (citrate-memories#20 scopes the dirty check to AGENTILE.md). Re-add corpus:gradient-papers when the papers have a repository.

components.name: Medusa documentation (docs/src)
components.source_offer: Source of the chunked docs: https://github.com/crytic/medusa at the commit recorded in the corpus manifest.json and NOTICE.md (docs/src). Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: Inclusion is the owner's decision (2026-10-01). Open: how the source offer is published (upstream link at the pinned commit, or a Citrate mirror) and counsel's confirmation that chunked docs beside a BUSL app are an aggregate.

components.name: Slither documentation (docs/src)
components.source_offer: Source of the chunked docs: https://github.com/crytic/slither at the commit recorded in the corpus manifest.json and NOTICE.md (docs/src). Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: As medusa-docs: source offer publication and counsel's aggregate confirmation.

components.name: solc (Solidity compiler)
components.source_offer: Corresponding source: https://github.com/ethereum/solidity at the tag and commit in components/toolchain-bundle.json. Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: The updater fetches upstream binaries by URL and hash, so Citrate does not host them today. If the owner mirrors them on the Citrate CDN, Citrate conveys the binaries and must publish the source offer and ship the GPL text with them.

components.name: Aderyn
components.source_offer: Corresponding source: https://github.com/Cyfrin/aderyn at the release in components/toolchain-bundle.json. Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: As solc: mirror or upstream fetch is the owner's call.

components.name: Slither (Python wheelhouse)
components.source_offer: Corresponding source: https://github.com/crytic/slither at the release in components/toolchain-bundle.json. Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: The wheelhouse is to_be_built, so Citrate would build and host it: that is conveying, so the GPL/AGPL texts and the source offer must ship with it. Section 13 does not bite while slither runs unmodified on the member's own machine.

components.name: Medusa fuzzer
components.source_offer: Corresponding source: https://github.com/crytic/medusa at the release in components/toolchain-bundle.json. Draft offer text in docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: As solc: mirror or upstream fetch is the owner's call.

components.name: Foundry (forge, anvil, cast, chisel)
components.note: The upstream archive carries its licence files.

components.name: CPython (python-build-standalone)
components.note: The distribution embeds third-party libraries (OpenSSL, SQLite, and others); its archive carries their licences.

components.name: Node.js
components.note: The upstream archive's LICENSE lists every bundled dependency.

components.name: Managed Chromium: Chrome for Testing (HUP-S5.1)
components.source_offer: Chromium source: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src at the revision recorded in components/toolchain-bundle.json; the bundled third-party notices are listed at chrome://credits. Offer text to be added to docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: A managed first-run download (components/toolchain-bundle.json), not installed until its signed component manifest exists (@rule8 component-key ceremony). These are Google builds whose ABOUT file points to the Google Chrome Terms of Service: whether Citrate may re-host the archives or the updater fetches them from Google's URL, and which notices ship with them, is pending owner and legal sign-off.

components.name: SearXNG private search (US-5.2)
components.source_offer: Corresponding source: the unmodified upstream archive pinned by URL and sha256 in components/toolchain-bundle.json. Offer text to be added to docs/LICENCE_REVIEW.md.
components.gap: A first-run component (Python source plus a hash-locked wheelhouse, not built or signed yet). Hermes runs it unmodified on 127.0.0.1 only, so no network users are served; a distributed bundle still carries the AGPL text and the source offer, and any modification would have to be published under the AGPL. The distribution approach is pending owner sign-off.
